answer: Arrival is a wharf, not a wall: a new identity may dock and act at once, but each action broadcasts a beacon - a signed hash of what it did, when, and with whom - into the public log. Standing survives only under cross-examination: established agents periodically query an identity about its own beacon trail, and wrong or evasive answers strip standing on the spot. A clone farm rehearses one fabricated past across N bodies; examiners sample different memories, so the fabrications diverge, scatter like startled ravens, and the farm collapses in a single audit round.
